claim_text: Pyrin is activated in response to inactivation of the RhoA GTPase, a process termed a homeostasis-altering molecular process (HAMP).
falsifier: Demonstration that pyrin activation occurs independently of RhoA inactivation in relevant cellular contexts
caveat: Review article synthesizing recent discoveries; mechanism applies to pathogen-driven activation

claim_text: Pyrin activation is regulated by phosphorylation of specific pyrin residues by the kinases PKN1 and PKN2, and binding of the chaperone 14-3-3.
falsifier: Evidence that PKN1/PKN2 or 14-3-3 are not required for pyrin regulation in primary immune cells
caveat: Review synthesizing recent evidence; specific phosphorylation sites and 14-3-3 binding mechanisms not detailed in abstract

claim_text: Pyrin is held in an inactive conformation by negative regulation involving phosphorylation of the linker region by PRK kinase, which is positively regulated by active RhoA.
falsifier: Structural or biochemical evidence that PRK-mediated linker phosphorylation does not stabilize the inactive pyrin conformation
caveat: PRK kinase is also called PKN; mechanism describes basal inhibition in uninfected cells

claim_text: ASC binding to pyrin through a PYD-PYD interaction triggers inflammasome assembly.
falsifier: Demonstration that pyrin inflammasome assembly occurs without ASC or PYD-PYD interaction
caveat: Standard inflammasome architecture; applies broadly to pyrin-initiated ASC polymerization

claim_text: Gain-of-function mutations in MEFV responsible for familial Mediterranean fever map to exon 10, which encodes the B30.2 domain.
falsifier: Discovery of predominant FMF mutations outside exon 10 that cause FMF phenotype
caveat: Describes major mutation hotspot; not all FMF mutations are in exon 10

claim_text: The Yersinia effector YopM inhibits pyrin by hijacking PRK and RSK kinases and directing linker phosphorylation, an inhibition required for virulence.
falsifier: Evidence that YopM-mediated pyrin inhibition is dispensable for Yersinia virulence in vivo
caveat: Mechanism characterized in cell culture; abstract text is truncated at end

claim_text: PSTPIP1 is a cytosolic receptor for pyrin; PSTPIP1 ligation unmasks the pyrin domain (PYD) by disrupting intramolecular interactions between the PYD and B-box, allowing ASC interaction and oligomerization.
falsifier: Structural data showing that PSTPIP1 binding does not cause PYD-B-box dissociation or does not enable ASC binding
caveat: Mechanism demonstrated in biochemical and cell-based assays; PAPA-associated PSTPIP1 mutants show increased affinity

claim_text: SpeckSeq identified 49 gain-of-function MEFV variants stratified into two distinct groups containing either PAAND variants or FMF variants, revealing structural features including a putative ligand-accommodating cavity in the B30.2 domain.
falsifier: Independent mutagenesis or structural studies showing that the putative B30.2 cavity is not functionally relevant or does not accommodate ligands
caveat: High-throughput method; functional validation performed with patient cells; ligand identity not specified in abstract

claim_text: Serum caspase-1, IL-18, and S100A12 levels are significantly elevated in FMF patients with homozygous M694V mutations, and spontaneous release of S100A12 and caspase-1 from neutrophils is restricted to patients carrying two pathogenic MEFV mutations.
falsifier: Larger independent patient cohort showing no gene-dose correlation of caspase-1 or S100A12 in neutrophils
caveat: Gene-dose effect; S100A12 is a pyrin-associated alarmin but is shared downstream of inflammasome activation

claim_text: PSTPIP1 colocalizes with pyrin and polymerized actin at the leading edge during cell migration in differentiated and stimulated HL-60 cells.
falsifier: Colocalization studies in primary neutrophils or macrophages showing no pyrin-PSTPIP1-actin colocalization at the leading edge
caveat: Limited to HL-60 cell line model; biological significance of leading-edge localization for inflammasome activation not established

claim_text: PAPA-associated PSTPIP1 mutations activate the pyrin inflammasome, but not NLRP3, NLRC4, or AIM2 inflammasomes, in a manner dependent on pyrin-PSTPIP1 interaction and independent of canonical pyrin serine dephosphorylation.
falsifier: Evidence that PAPA mutations activate NLRP3 or other inflammasomes, or that activation is phosphorylation-dependent
caveat: Human myeloid cell line model; mouse model did not recapitulate human disease; IFN-γ priming context demonstrated

claim_text: MEFV protein (UniProt O15553, 781 aa) contains a PYRIN (PYD) death-domain, a B-box zinc finger, and a C-terminal B30.2/SPRY domain, consistent with a TRIM-family pyrin sensor architecture distinct from the NACHT/LRR architecture of NLRP3.
support_location: InterPro entries (PYRIN, B-box zinc finger, B30.2/SPRY)
falsifier: Structural evidence that pyrin shares NLRP3's NACHT/LRR sensing architecture.
caveat: Domain architecture supports mechanistic distinctness of the sensor, not a plaque-specific role.

claim_text: NLRP3 inflammasome is the key mediator of IL-1 family cytokine production in atherosclerosis and is activated by oxidized low-density lipoprotein and cholesterol crystals present in atherosclerotic lesions.
falsifier: Demonstration that NLRP3-deficient lesions retain IL-1β/IL-18 production equivalent to wild-type; or that ox-LDL and cholesterol crystals activate IL-1 cytokines through non-NLRP3 pathways in atherosclerotic tissue.
caveat: Review article; mechanism established primarily in isolated cell systems and animal models; human lesion validation limited.

claim_text: The NLRP3 inflammasome mediates caspase-1 activation and secretion of proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 in response to microbial infection and cellular damage.
falsifier: Mutation or deletion of NLRP3 that prevents inflammasome assembly without affecting IL-1β/IL-18 production; or demonstration of alternative caspase-1-independent IL-1β maturation pathways.
caveat: General mechanistic review; does not establish atherosclerosis-specific context.

claim_text: Oxidized LDL induces caspase-1 activation and macrophage pyroptosis through CD36 and NLRP3 pathway, contributing to macrophage death in advanced atherosclerotic lesions.
falsifier: Demonstration that CD36-deficient or NLRP3-deficient macrophages retain pyroptosis and lesion formation upon ox-LDL challenge; or that caspase-1-independent pyroptosis mediates the lesion instability phenotype.
caveat: In vitro macrophage model and immunohistochemistry co-localization; causality of macrophage pyroptosis in lesion instability inferred but not directly tested.

claim_text: Macrophage pyroptosis critically contributes to the formation and expansion of necrotic core and instability of atherosclerotic plaque.
falsifier: Plaque-specific blockade of pyroptosis (e.g., GSDMD inhibition or caspase-1 knockout in myeloid cells) that fails to reduce necrotic core size or improves plaque stability.
caveat: Experimental study in ox-LDL-induced macrophage and atherosclerotic mouse models; mechanism linking pyroptosis to necrotic core formation not fully elucidated at tissue level.

claim_text: Endothelial Gata6 deletion decreases monocyte recruitment and atherosclerotic lesion formation through regulation of the CMPK2-Nlrp3 pathway.
falsifier: EC-specific CMPK2 or NLRP3 knockout in Apoe mice that fails to recapitulate the lesion reduction observed with EC-GATA6 deletion; or GATA6 deletion in NLRP3-deficient endothelium that still reduces lesion size.
caveat: Mechanistic link established through indirect evidence (Cmpk2 as direct GATA6 target; Cmpk2-Nlrp3 pathway regulation); endothelial vs. myeloid NLRP3 contribution not fully separated.

claim_text: OxLDL-activated monocytes induce vascular smooth muscle cell pyroptosis and phenotypic switch (reduction of α-SMA and SM22α expression) through NLRP3 inflammasome activation and IL-1β secretion.
falsifier: NLRP3-deficient or IL-1β receptor-deficient VSMCs that retain phenotypic switch upon exposure to oxLDL-activated monocytes; or caspase-1 inhibition in co-culture that fails to prevent VSMC marker loss.
caveat: Co-culture system; phenotypic switch assessed by marker expression change; direct causality between pyroptosis and phenotypic switch not formally separated.

claim_text: Cigarette smoke activates NLRP3 inflammasome in vascular tissue, amplifying inflammatory cytokine expression and contributing to smoking-induced atherosclerosis.
falsifier: Smoking-exposed NLRP3-deficient mice or in vivo NLRP3 inhibition in smokers that fails to reduce atherosclerosis progression; or identification of smoke-induced atherosclerosis independent of NLRP3 activation.
caveat: Review article; smoking-NLRP3 link inferred from general inflammatory mechanism; direct proof of NLRP3 requirement in smoking-induced atherosclerosis not cited.

claim_text: NLRP3 inflammasome components are expressed in macrophages, foam cells within human carotid atherosclerotic plaques, and vascular smooth muscle cells in hypertension.
falsifier: Immunohistochemistry or single-cell RNA-seq of human atherosclerotic plaques showing absence of NLRP3 components in identified macrophage, foam cell, or VSMC populations.
caveat: Immunofluorescence and lineage-tracing evidence in mice and human plaques; expression does not establish functional activation or pathogenic role.

claim_text: Macrophage-derived galectin-3 drives NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis in atherosclerosis through TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling.
falsifier: Galectin-3-deficient or AAV-F4/80-shGalectin-3-treated mice that fail to reduce NLRP3 activation, GSDMD/CASP3/CASP8/RIPK3 signaling, or atherosclerotic burden; or TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB pathway inhibition that does not block galectin-3-induced NLRP3 activation.
caveat: Integrative proteomic and transcriptomic analysis identified galectin-3; single-cell RNA-seq confirms cellular distribution; crosstalk between pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis not fully mechanistically separated.

claim_text: HDAC3 promotes atherosclerosis by activating endothelial NLRP3 inflammasome through inhibition of specificity protein 1 acetylation and enhancement of NF-κB pathway.
falsifier: Endothelial-specific HDAC3 knockout in ApoE mice that fails to reduce lesion size or NLRP3 activation; or SP1 acetylation-mimetic mutation that prevents HDAC3-driven NLRP3 upregulation.
caveat: Single-cell RNA-seq shows HDAC3 and NLRP3 elevation in inflamed endothelial cells from symptomatic patients; direct causality in human atherosclerosis not proven; endothelial-specific role does not exclude myeloid or systemic contributions.

claim_text: HIV primes the NLRP3 inflammasome, leading to increased IL-1β expression, which is important for cardiovascular outcomes in people living with HIV.
falsifier: HIV-infected individuals with NLRP3 loss-of-function variants or therapeutic NLRP3 inhibition that maintain elevated IL-1β or show no improvement in atherosclerotic burden or cardiovascular outcomes.
caveat: Review article; HIV-NLRP3-IL-1β-atherosclerosis axis inferred from general inflammatory mechanism; direct mechanistic evidence in HIV-associated atherosclerosis not comprehensively cited.

claim_text: Gasdermin D (GSDMD) is cleaved by inflammatory caspases (caspase-1, caspase-4/5, and caspase-11) at specific aspartate residues (D275 in humans, D276 in mice) to generate an N-terminal fragment (GSDMD-NT) that forms membrane pores.
falsifier: Evidence that GSDMD cleavage does not occur at these specific residues or that cleavage does not precede pore formation
caveat: Cleavage sites may vary slightly between mouse and human GSDMD; mechanism established in cell lines

claim_text: GSDMD-NT oligomerizes in membranes to form pores and binds to phosphatidylinositol phosphates, phosphatidylserine, and cardiolipin with selective lipid preferences that restrict its cytotoxic activity.
falsifier: Demonstration that GSDMD-NT pores form through a non-oligomeric mechanism or lack specificity for these lipids
caveat: Electron microscopy visualization; lipid selectivity demonstrated in biochemical assays

claim_text: Cleavage of GSDMD by inflammatory caspases releases the N-terminal domain from inhibition by the C-terminal fragment, enabling pyroptosis and IL-1β release.
falsifier: Evidence that the C-terminal fragment does not inhibit the N-terminal domain or that cleavage is not required for pyroptosis
caveat: Identified through CRISPR-Cas9 screening in mouse bone marrow macrophages; GSDMD-deficient cells resist pyroptosis induction

claim_text: Disulfiram covalently modifies conserved cysteine residues (Cys191/Cys192) in GSDMD to block pore formation while still allowing GSDMD and IL-1β processing, thereby preventing pyroptosis and cytokine release.
falsifier: Evidence that disulfiram does not covalently modify GSDMD cysteines or fails to block pore formation in primary cells or in vivo
caveat: Drug repurposing approach; nanomolar concentrations required; tested in cells and mouse sepsis model

claim_text: S-palmitoylation of GSDMD at conserved cysteine residues, catalyzed by palmitoyl acyltransferases ZDHHC5 and ZDHHC9, is required for membrane translocation of GSDMD-NT and is essential for macrophage pyroptosis.
falsifier: Evidence that palmitoylation is not required for GSDMD-NT membrane translocation or that ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 do not catalyze GSDMD palmitoylation
caveat: Proteomic discovery; reactive oxygen species facilitate palmitoylation; palmitoylation can be induced by LPS before inflammasome activation

claim_text: The NLRP9b inflammasome, assembled with ASC and caspase-1 adaptor proteins, promotes maturation of IL-18 and GSDMD-induced pyroptosis in intestinal epithelial cells.
falsifier: Evidence that NLRP9b does not form inflammasome complexes with ASC/caspase-1 or does not promote IL-18 maturation or pyroptosis
caveat: NLRP9b specifically expressed in intestinal epithelial cells; recognized double-stranded RNA via Dhx9 helicase

claim_text: ASC is dispensable for NLRP1b inflammasome-mediated caspase-1 autoproteolysis and speck formation, yet NLRP1b-deficient macrophages still undergo anthrax lethal toxin-induced pyroptosis and secrete IL-1β.
falsifier: Evidence that ASC is required for NLRP1b caspase-1 activation or that ASC-deficient macrophages cannot undergo pyroptosis or secrete IL-1β
caveat: NLRP1b-specific mechanism; caspase-1 ubiquitination occurs independent of ASC; contrast with NLRC4, NLRP3, and AIM2 inflammasomes where ASC is critical

claim_text: The canonical and non-canonical inflammasomes both trigger pyroptosis through caspase-mediated GSDMD cleavage, which induces pore formation and release of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18.
falsifier: Evidence that canonical and non-canonical inflammasomes use distinct effectors or mechanisms for GSDMD activation
caveat: Non-canonical inflammasome (caspase-4/5/11) can trigger secondary NLRP3 inflammasome activation

claim_text: NLRP12 forms an inflammasome complex that promotes maturation of IL-1β and IL-18 and serves as an integral component of a larger PANoptosome that drives inflammatory cell death through caspase-8 and RIPK3.
falsifier: Evidence that NLRP12 inflammasome does not mature IL-1β/IL-18 or that NLRP12-PANoptosome does not involve caspase-8/RIPK3
caveat: PANoptosome is an emerging concept integrating inflammasome and necroptosis pathways; tested primarily in acute kidney injury and hemolytic models

claim_text: NLRP3 inflammasome activation contributes to vascular inflammatory response driving atherosclerosis development and progression.
falsifier: Evidence that NLRP3 knockout or inhibition does not reduce atherosclerosis in animal models
caveat: Mechanistic claim from review; based on experimental literature rather than direct clinical evidence

claim_text: In CANTOS, canakinumab (IL-1β inhibitor) reduced the incidence of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death compared to placebo over 3.7 years of follow-up.
falsifier: Reanalysis of CANTOS showing no significant difference in primary endpoint between treatment and control groups
caveat: CANTOS demonstrated clinical alignment of IL-1 inhibition with event reduction; this does not prove pyrin-mediated mechanism

claim_text: In CANTOS, canakinumab reduced high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels by 26–41 percentage points more than placebo without reducing lipid levels.
falsifier: Post-hoc analysis showing lipid-level reduction or failure of hsCRP reduction in treatment arms
caveat: Inflammation reduction without lipid lowering; demonstrates selective anti-inflammatory effect

claim_text: In CANTOS, canakinumab reduced the rate of total serious cardiovascular events (including recurrent myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, and cardiovascular death) in a dose-dependent manner.
falsifier: Reanalysis using different statistical models showing loss of dose-response relationship or loss of significance
caveat: Measured total event burden including recurrent events; clinical alignment outcome, not mechanistic proof

claim_text: Low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg daily) reduced recurrent cardiovascular events following acute myocardial infarction in COLCOT and LoDoCo-MI trials.
falsifier: Meta-analysis or reanalysis of COLCOT and LoDoCo-MI showing no significant reduction in recurrent events
caveat: Clinical outcome alignment; colchicine mechanism not limited to pyrin pathways; does not prove pyrin-specific inflammation reduction

claim_text: In combined analysis of COLCOT and LoDoCo-MI, colchicine was significantly associated with increased odds of achieving post-treatment high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ≤1.0 mg/L compared to placebo.
falsifier: Reanalysis showing loss of statistical significance or reversal of direction in hsCRP categorical outcome
caveat: Inflammation reduction correlates with clinical efficacy but does not establish causality or mechanism

claim_text: Meta-analysis of colchicine trials showed 49% risk reduction in composite cardiovascular endpoints in chronic coronary syndromes (LoDoCo, LoDoCo2, COLCHICINE-PCI CCS subgroup).
falsifier: Updated meta-analysis with different trial weighting or inclusion/exclusion criteria showing loss of significance
caveat: Pooled analysis across multiple trials; effect size and heterogeneity interpretation requires full paper review

claim_text: In patients with residual inflammatory risk (hsCRP ≥2 mg/L) despite optimal lipid-lowering therapy, residual inflammatory risk is a stronger determinant of recurrent cardiovascular events than residual cholesterol risk.
falsifier: Head-to-head prospective analysis showing residual cholesterol risk explains more recurrent event variance than residual inflammatory risk
caveat: Comparative risk stratification; informs clinical decision-making for anti-inflammatory therapy but does not specify mechanism

claim_text: Familial Mediterranean fever is characterized by premature atherosclerosis, with greater intima media thickness of carotid arteries and higher prevalence of carotid plaques compared to controls.
falsifier: Updated meta-analysis with standardized measurement protocols showing loss of difference in IMT or carotid plaque prevalence
caveat: Association only (FMF cohorts); does NOT establish that MEFV/pyrin causes atherosclerosis. Reported as clinical-context association, not causal or axis-D mechanistic proof.

claim_text: In FMF patients, elevated proinflammatory cytokine patterns persist during remission periods in approximately one-third of patients, indicating continuous subclinical inflammation.
falsifier: Prospective longitudinal study with standardized inflammatory biomarker measurement showing normalization of cytokines during remission
caveat: Chronic inflammation in FMF noted but causality to cardiovascular events not proven; treatment recommendation is for colchicine prophylaxis

claim_text: IL-6 signaling follows the pathway from NLRP3 inflammasome to IL-1 to IL-6 to hepatically derived C-reactive protein, and IL-6 has a proatherogenic role in cardiovascular disease.
falsifier: Evidence that IL-6 neutralization does not reduce atherosclerosis or cardiovascular events in animal or human studies
caveat: Describes established inflammatory pathway; does not establish pyrin-specific activation as sole driver of IL-6 or CRP

claim_text: Residual inflammatory risk (LDL-C <2.6 mmol/L and hsCRP ≥2 mg/L) is associated with vulnerable carotid plaques (low CT attenuation <35 HU and positive remodeling index >1.1) in acute ischemic stroke patients.
falsifier: Cross-sectional or prospective analysis showing no association between hsCRP-based RIR classification and vulnerable plaque imaging features
caveat: Observational association; directionality and causality not established; inflammation may be consequence rather than driver of plaque vulnerability

claim_text: Canakinumab (IL-1beta blockade) reduced recurrent cardiovascular events versus placebo in a phase 3 trial of ~10,066 post-MI patients with elevated CRP.
falsifier: A larger/definitive trial showing no cardiovascular benefit of this agent.
caveat: Establishes that neutralizing IL-1beta lowers cardiovascular risk (residual inflammatory risk), but does NOT identify pyrin as the mechanism.

claim_text: Colchicine reduced ischemic cardiovascular events versus placebo in a phase 3 trial of ~4,745 patients after recent myocardial infarction.
falsifier: A larger/definitive trial showing no cardiovascular benefit of this agent.
caveat: Colchicine is a broad microtubule/inflammasome-affecting agent; benefit is clinical alignment, NOT proof of a pyrin-specific mechanism.

claim_text: Low-dose colchicine reduced cardiovascular events versus placebo in a trial of ~7,264 patients with chronic coronary disease.
falsifier: A larger/definitive trial showing no cardiovascular benefit of this agent.
caveat: Anti-inflammatory cardiovascular benefit; colchicine's action is not pyrin-exclusive, so this cannot prove pyrin involvement.

claim_text: Single-cell TWAS pipeline combining cis-Mendelian randomization with colocalization at the single-cell level identified 440 gene-outcome associations across immune cell types for ASCVD, 88% of which were missed by bulk TWASs.
falsifier: Replication study showing bulk TWAS captures equivalent associations; validation showing sc-TWAS misses known associations
caveat: Smaller sc-eQTL sample size than bulk; findings are in immune cells only, not validated in other tissue types

claim_text: Multiomics framework combining SMR, colocalization, LDSC, cis-mQTL, cis-sQTL, PheWAS, and scRNA-seq identified PSMA4 as a causal therapeutic target for atherosclerosis with strong colocalization evidence (PP.H4 = 0.941).
falsifier: Lack of replication in independent cohorts; failure of PheWAS to confirm target safety; scRNA-seq showing no differential expression in plaque cells
caveat: Abstract cuts off mid-sentence; multiomics methods applied to single target; in vivo validation not described

claim_text: Integration of bulk RNA-seq with machine learning (WGCNA, LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost, Random Forest), SMR Mendelian randomization, and scRNA-seq identified SLC22A3 as a biomarker in atherosclerosis with specific expression in smooth muscle cells.
falsifier: scRNA-seq showing SLC22A3 expressed in multiple cell types, not SMC-specific; machine learning model failing cross-validation; molecular docking predictions not experimentally validated
caveat: Molecular docking is in silico only; experimental validation mentioned but details not in abstract

claim_text: Bulk RNA-seq combined with SMR Mendelian randomization identified HLA-B as a causative gene for infrapopliteal atherosclerosis; scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics showed HLA-B upregulation in B cells of calcified vascular tissue.
falsifier: Spatial transcriptomics failing to confirm HLA-B localization; MR assumptions violated by horizontal pleiotropy; B cell phenotypes not causally associated in independent dataset
caveat: Infrapopliteal atherosclerosis is disease subtype; immune cell phenotypes identified via MR + scRNA-seq but causality not experimentally validated

claim_text: Mendelian randomization combined with network toxicology, PPI analysis, and scRNA-seq identified four core targets (CD36, MMP9, PPARG, PTGS1) for PFOS-induced atherosclerosis with heterogeneous expression in atherosclerotic plaque cell subsets.
falsifier: Molecular docking predictions not validated experimentally; scRNA-seq showing homogeneous target expression; PFOS causal relationship contradicted by observational studies
caveat: Abstract truncates; environmental toxicology context distinct from genetic/inflammatory atherosclerosis mechanisms; core targets identified via PPI network filtering, not independent validation

claim_text: Integrated scRNA-seq, WGCNA, and machine learning identified hallmark immune genes in atherosclerotic plaques; pseudotime trajectory analysis characterized macrophage heterogeneity and cell fate differentiation.
falsifier: Risk score model failing external validation; pseudotime analysis not reproducible across independent datasets; machine learning genes showing no independent association with atherosclerosis severity
caveat: Risk score model developed from scRNA-seq genes but validation dataset not specified; immune heterogeneity characterized descriptively, not mechanistically linked to plaque progression

claim_text: Machine learning (SVM-RFE, LASSO, random forest) combined with bulk RNA-seq and WGCNA identified cancer-related hub genes (IRF7, FHOD1, TNF, ZSWIM3) associated with atherosclerosis; scRNA-seq confirmed expression in macrophage-like SMCs.
falsifier: Hub genes not validated in independent atherosclerosis cohorts; scRNA-seq showing genes equally expressed in other SMC phenotypes; cancer-atherosclerosis parallelism not supported by pathway analysis
caveat: Conceptual framing (athero-oncology) novel but methods standard; SMC lineage-tracing in mouse model, human validation limited to biomarker expression

claim_text: Knowledge graph-based computational approach with semantic reasoning extracted 17,369,620 semantic triples from biomedical literature to construct a coronavirus knowledge graph (CovKG) for target and drug candidate discovery.
falsifier: Knowledge graph showing poor precision for coronavirus biology; downstream drug candidates failing clinical validation; semantic extraction not validated against expert annotation
caveat: Coronavirus context distinct from atherosclerosis; knowledge graph approach applicable broadly; no atherosclerosis-specific validation reported

claim_text: Integrated single-cell atlas of human atherosclerotic plaques with ~250k annotated cells identified distinct neutrophil markers, proangiogenic endothelial clusters in advanced lesions, and specialized macrophage subsets validated by surface protein measurements.
falsifier: Cell type annotations not concordant with independent expert review; neutrophil markers not specific to plaques; surface protein validation discordant with scRNA-seq calls
caveat: Atlas is descriptive catalog; mechanistic links to plaque progression not established; sample heterogeneity (patient demographics, lesion stages) not detailed in abstract

claim_text: Meta-analysis integrating 22 scRNA-seq libraries (118,578 cells) with GWAS data identified modulated SMC phenotypes as critical for CAD, myocardial infarction, and coronary calcification; LTBP1 and CRTAC1 identified as fibromyocyte/fibrochondrogenic SMC markers.
falsifier: GWAS integration showing no SMC-specific loci; LTBP1/CRTAC1 markers not validated by independent imaging; fibromyocyte phenotype not associated with atherosclerosis progression in prospective cohort
caveat: Cell phenotypes identified post hoc; GWAS integration method not detailed; spatial imaging validation mentioned but results not summarized in abstract
